title: quest init checks for the opum-quest plugin when the Claude or Codex target is selected; agents --update-instructions converges on the marketplace
description: ADR gap 1, rulings (a)-(c), at opum-doc main 2112fc6, docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md (operator ruling 2026-09-25T14:09:02.971Z, dispatched by opum-agent as OPAG-421). Today quest init and quest agents only DOCUMENT skillSource=plugin (agent-instructions.ts:274-290, command-help.ts); nothing checks whether opum-quest is installed. (a) When quest init selects the claude or codex target, it checks for the opum-quest marketplace plugin. (b) Once the plugin is installed, the marketplace is the skill's update channel, and quest agents does not regenerate a plugin-sourced skill. (c) quest agents --update-instructions also pulls from the marketplace, so the repo-copy path and the plugin path converge on one source. The detection mechanism is our call, but it must be IDENTICAL to lore-cli's (ruling d): agree it with the lore-cli session first. Open questions to route if the ADR does not settle them: what the check does for Codex, since opum-quest is a Claude Code plugin; and whether pulling from the marketplace puts network access into an otherwise LLM-free, local CLI.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest init with the claude or codex target reports whether opum-quest is installed, by the mechanism agreed with lore-cli, proven by a test covering both installed and absent
A plugin-sourced skill is not regenerated by quest agents, and the marketplace is named as its update channel
quest agents --update-instructions draws the skill from the marketplace source, so the repo-generated and plugin copies cannot silently diverge
The mechanism matches lore-cli's in detection method, init check point and update convergence, cited against lore-cli's implementing commit

plan: 1. Port src/ports/agent-plugins.ts: AgentPluginPort.list(runtime) returns the listed plugins (id, enabled, version) or unavailable; update(runtime, id) runs the runtime update and reports ok and detail

2. Adapter src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts shells out to the PUBLIC list commands only: claude plugin list --json (rows id/enabled/version) and codex plugin list --json (.installed[] pluginId/enabled/version). Update is claude plugin update opum-quest@opum, or codex plugin marketplace upgrade opum then codex plugin add opum-quest@opum (Codex has no plugin update; measured). Short timeout for list, long for update

3. Application src/application/agents/agent-plugins.ts: four states per ADR Amendment 2 (installed, disabled, not-installed, not-detectable), plus the remedy to print: install, enable (Codex has no enable command, so the config.toml key is named) or update. The claude target maps to claude and codex to codex; antigravity gets no plugin check
4. init: after target selection and before the instruction and skill writes, detect for each selected claude/codex target and report data.plugins.<runtime>. Never mutates; no exit-code change
5. agents --check: report data.plugin for the target runtime. Never mutates; no exit-code change

6. agents --update-instructions: if installed, RUN the update and report its outcome; if disabled, never enable, report and print the enable command; otherwise report and print install. The repo-copy skill path is unchanged
7. Tests hermetic via fake claude/codex on PATH, covering every state x command plus a missing binary; bun run check; tell lore-cli the exact mechanism for ruling (d)
implementationNotes: BINDING INPUTS, as of 2026-09-25. (1) ADR Amendment 1, opum-doc main ac8dd7b: Codex is in scope now. init and --check detect, report and print the command, and never mutate. agents --update-instructions runs the plugin update itself when the plugin is installed. (2) opum-agent ruling on the state set, 14:53Z, NOT YET BINDING: it binds once opum-doc records it as a further amendment, so read that record before building. FOUR states: installed, disabled (installed with enabled:false, never reported as installed), not installed, not detectable. init and --check report disabled and print the enable command. The manual update command NEVER enables a disabled plugin: it reports disabled and prints the enable command. On Codex, disabled is reported only if Codex own plugin commands expose enablement; otherwise Codex has three states, and nothing synthesises the fourth. MEASURED here, codex-cli 0.155.1: `codex plugin` has add, list, marketplace and remove, and no enable or disable subcommand. Its --enable/--disable options toggle Codex FEATURES (features.<name>), not plugins. Whether `codex plugin list --json` rows carry an enabled field is UNMEASURED, because no opum plugin is installed under Codex and installing one would mutate the user Codex config; re-measure once opum-marketplace makes the Codex listing resolve. Claude side, measured: `claude plugin list --json` rows carry enabled and version. lore-cli has not yet read the mechanism proposal; it is held behind an operator-only question. opum-agent will amend the ruling if lore-cli argues it.

MEASURED 2026-09-25 in an isolated CODEX_HOME (scratch, not the user config), codex-cli 0.155.1: marketplace add opum-ai/opum-marketplace, then plugin add opum-quest@opum, installed 0.10.0 (opum-marketplace has since fixed resolution). The .installed[] row key set is [authPolicy, enabled, installPolicy, installed, marketplaceName, marketplaceSource, name, pluginId, source, version]. With [plugins."opum-quest@opum"] enabled = false in config.toml, the row reads installed:true, enabled:false. So Codex EXPOSES enablement, and under ruling 22 the Codex side has all four states. Codex has no plugin enable or update command. Update equivalent: codex plugin marketplace upgrade opum (exit 0, took over 120s: a git fetch) then codex plugin add opum-quest@opum (exit 0, idempotent). Latency: claude plugin list --json 0.14s, codex plugin list --json 0.44s. Claude rows carry id, enabled, version; claude plugin enable <id> exists.

IMPLEMENTED, built to opum-doc main b6358e7 (ADR rulings (a)-(c), Amendment 1 rulings 18-19, Amendment 2 rulings 20-22). New port src/ports/agent-plugins.ts; adapter src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts, which calls only the public `claude plugin list --json` (rows id/enabled/version) and `codex plugin list --json` (.installed[] pluginId/enabled/version), with a 15s list timeout and a 600s update timeout; application src/application/agents/agent-plugins.ts, with four states and a remedy for each. PAYLOAD (additive, under data): init has plugins.<claude|codex> for each selected claude or codex target, detected BEFORE the instruction and skill writes; agents --check and --update-instructions have plugin for the target runtime (a bare call is codex; antigravity has none). --update-instructions runs `claude plugin update opum-quest@opum`, or `codex plugin marketplace upgrade opum` then `codex plugin add opum-quest@opum`, ONLY when the plugin is installed, and reports update ran/not-run plus updateOk/updateDetail. It never installs or enables. A failed update keeps exit 0 (the instructions update succeeded) and reports updateOk:false with the command to rerun. No exit code changes anywhere. The repo-copy skill path is unchanged: skillSource still governs it. DECISIONS OF MINE, flagged for ruling (d) parity with lore-cli: (1) state strings are kebab-case (installed, disabled, not-installed, not-detectable), matching quest's existing version-only; (2) QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS=off makes every check not-detectable and starts no runtime. It exists because the test suite spawns the real CLI, and without it `agents --update-instructions` in any test would update the developer's real installed plugin. bunfig.toml preloads it for the suite; the QCLI-371 tests unset it and use fake binaries. (3) The Codex enable remedy names the config.toml key, because Codex has no enable command. TESTS test/qcli371-marketplace-plugin-check.test.ts, 14 cases, hermetic via fake claude/codex on PATH that log every call: each runtime x four states; disabled never reads as installed; --check runs only the list; --update-instructions runs exactly the update steps for installed and nothing but the list for disabled or not-installed; a failed update; a missing binary is not-detectable; init per target; antigravity starts no runtime; the off switch. CONTROLS (mutations of the check, with predictions): C1 disabled folded into installed, 7/14 red, as predicted. C2 the update never runs, 4/14, as predicted. C3 the off switch ignored, 1/14, as predicted. C4 unavailable folded into not-installed: predicted 3, got 4. The 4th is the off-switch case, which asserts not-detectable and so depends on the same branch; the prediction missed it, and the test is correct. Clean 14/14. bun run check exit 0, 637 pass. Real-binary smoke (--check only): claude reports installed 0.7.1, codex reports not-installed, and claude off PATH reports not-detectable. The real opum-quest plugin was untouched by the suite (lastUpdated still 2026-09-24T04:11:01.193Z).

AC4 LEFT OPEN on purpose: it asks for parity cited against lore-cli's implementing commit, and lore-cli has not implemented yet (it is held behind an operator-only question). The mechanism was sent to lore-cli on 2026-09-25, and opum-agent will amend the ADR if lore argues it. This task stays In Progress until that citation exists.

REVIEW (opum-workflow reviewer on #266 head 2f03278) and its disposition. (1) HIGH, test isolation leaked: an env-less spawn gets the ORIGINAL environment, which drops the preload variable. The reviewer measured 2 real `claude plugin list` calls from test/qcli272. FIXED: package.json test and test:packages set QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS=off at the process boundary, prepublish.mjs passes it in every execFile env and in the candidate-smoke env, and qcli272 passes an explicit env. RE-MEASURED with logging fakes first on PATH: bun run test gave 0 calls, and plain bun test gave 0 calls (647 pass each). Positive control: the same fakes logged a call from one quest invocation with the variable unset, so zero is a real zero. (2) HIGH, latent: scripts/test-packed-packages.mjs would run a real Codex update on a release workstation. FIXED: it sets the variable at the top, and its package script sets it too. (3) MEDIUM, Claude scope: FIXED. The decoder drops local/project rows whose projectPath is not this project (realpath, or a prefix of it), picks the most specific applicable row (local > project > user > managed > synced), and reports scope; the update passes --scope. (4) MEDIUM-LOW, the timeout was not a hard bound: FIXED with its own deadline, a SIGKILL, and unref, without waiting on pipes a grandchild holds. (5) LOW, reason text: the signal case now names the signal. The EACCES case does not occur, because Bun resolves a bare name via PATH and skips a non-executable (measured: ENOENT "Executable not found in $PATH"); pinned by a test. (6) LOW: a non-empty list with no decodable row is now not-detectable, never not-installed. (7) LOW, a failing --check reports no plugin state: LEFT AS IS, because error envelopes carry no data, and adding a key there is a contract change, not a fix. (8) Routed to opum-agent, who ruled 25 (option A): a bare --update-instructions names no runtime, so it only reports; the Codex update output says it refreshed every opum plugin. BUILT. CONTROLS, one predicted case each, all exact: M1 projectPath filter removed, M2 first row wins, M3 a bare call runs the update, M4 undecodable read as empty, M5 no hard deadline; clean 24/24. My own first run of these controls printed no test output (a zsh unsplit $T), was caught by the missing summary line, and was re-run with an argv array. bun run check exit 0, 647 pass.
